hypothesis: Coincident numeric GL names in independent array/buffer namespaces can hide a native array/buffer field swap from the present headless seam.
source_behavior: gen_arrays and gen_buffers both initialize name=1 and choose the lowest unused name; create/delete always pair array and buffer objects in current traces.
Actual createMesh binds mesh->array as VAO and mesh->buffer as GL_ARRAY_BUFFER; updateMesh again binds mesh->buffer, and drawMesh binds mesh->array.
The fixture stores array_buffer[bound_array]=bound_buffer and separately captures buffer data/hash.
potentially_weak_assertions: update_expected asserts bound_buffer == expected[slot].buffer; expected buffer and array names are numerically equal under the current generators.
bind_buffer asserts buffers[name].used; an array-valued name can still denote a live same-numbered buffer in this seam.
draw verifies hash/length through the recorded array_buffer relation, so coincident numeric names can also hide the wrong original field.

operations: Upload independently packed three-vertex nondegenerate triangle

smallest_independent_control.oracle: Distinct non-overlapping GL namespaces are selected by the test seam; no renderer field is consulted to select names or expected association.
smallest_independent_control.negative_control: In a saved graphics.c copy replace the updateMesh buffer binding with mesh->array. Preserve a coincident-name control to determine whether that mutation survives; distinct names must reject it before upload. Also distinguish a createMesh binding swap as a separate mutation.
smallest_independent_control.expected_result_is_not_evidence: Correct production is expected to pass both namespaces; the wrong-field mutation is expected to survive coincident names and fail with distinct names. Neither outcome has been executed in this proposal.
